title: jnwb.jrsa._pearson/_spearman/_procrustes fabricated null-looking values on failure instead of failing loudly -- fixed, no live consumer affected

generated.summary: Three functions in jnwb/jrsa.py substituted a plausible-looking 'nothing here' value for a genuine computational failure, indistinguishable downstream from a real null result: (1) _pearson/_spearman returned (r=0, t=0, |r|=0, p=1.0, df=0) whenever jnwb.statistics.StatisticalAnalysis.correlate() reported {'error': 'Insufficient valid samples'} (n<3); (2) that same correlate() also silently rewrote NaN Pearson/Spearman statistics (e.g. from zero-variance/constant input) to statistic=0.0, pval=1.0; (3) _procrustes caught bare Exception from scipy.spatial.procrustes and fabricated disparity=1.0 (sim=0.0), which would also mask real bugs (shape errors, singular matrices) as 'maximally dissimilar'. Fixed: _pearson/_spearman now raise ValueError with the underlying reason and n; correlate() propagates NaN instead of rewriting it (NaN and 'measured zero, p=1' are different claims); _procrustes no longer catches the exception, so real scipy failures surface.

links.reasoning: Both are P0 items from the same 2026-08-15 PRGS instructions priority list (P0-A, P0-B); same session, same fabricated/incorrect-value class of bug though unrelated mechanisms.

notes: Blast radius at time of fix: no live script imports jnwb.jrsa and invokes metric='pearson'/'spearman'/'procrustes'. The only live importers (scripts/archive_oneoff/build_granger_connectivity_grid.py, scripts/archive_oneoff/suite_granger_v1_pfc.py) call only metric='granger', which does not go through _pearson/_spearman/_procrustes. No figure or headline number was corrupted by this bug as of 2026-08-17; the fix is a footgun closure in exported API, not a correction to a reported result. No corpus rerun was needed or performed for this reason.

jnwb/analyzers.py and jnwb/functions.py both call StatisticalAnalysis.correlate() and pass the result dict through unchanged (never unpack r_pearson/p_pearson-style flat keys, which don't exist on this API) -- the NaN-propagation change does not alter their behavior; confirmed by reading both call sites.

Known follow-up, deliberately not fixed in this cycle to keep scope narrow (per user direction): the CuPy/GPU branches of _pearson and _spearman still floor zero-variance input to r=0/rho=0 (jnwb/jrsa.py ~line 1018, ~1064) rather than propagating NaN, so the CPU and GPU paths now diverge on this specific degenerate case (they were coincidentally consistent before this fix, both mapping NaN->0). Not a regression introduced by this fix -- the GPU floor was pre-existing and untouched -- but worth revisiting for cross-backend consistency (numerical-computing skill) if the GPU path for these metrics is ever exercised on real data.
